title: Hardrock Course Description (2026)
claims: The 2026 course is 101.8 miles long with 33,441 feet of climb and 33,441 feet of descent, for 66,882 feet of total elevation change.
The course starts and finishes in Silverton and links the Lake City, Ouray, Telluride and Silverton areas in four legs.
The average elevation is about 11,000 feet and the high point is 14,048 feet.
There are 14 aid stations, with major aid stations in the towns and less well-equipped stations in between.
The course is closed, so runners are required to follow the specified route.
The organiser marks the entire course before the run, but long road sections and maintained trails may not be marked at all.
The altitude range is 7,700 to 14,000+ feet, with timberline locally at about 11,800 feet.
In a typical year runners have wet feet 90% or more of the run.
Every aid station is staffed by at least an EMT, has a first aid kit and has radio communication.
Each runner carries a SPOT tracker.
Runners who drop must inform the nearest Aid Station Captain and have their ID bracelet cut; transport from a dropout point may take many hours and is a best-effort arrangement.
The 48-hour cut-off allows runners to wait out thunderstorms or other life-threatening weather.

Recommended gear includes a hard-shell rain jacket, rain pants, emergency blanket, gloves, running hat, whistle, sunglasses, sunblock, a headlamp with backup, spare batteries, capacity to carry 80 oz of fluid and 500 calories.
The course page lists the 2026 clockwise course description and GPX file as updated 5 July 2026.
